idiom_name: owner goroutine or RWMutex-guarded state + channel/callback fan-out
implementation_notes: Go has no sealed unions and no broadcast stream, so the pattern is assembled from primitives: events as an interface with an unexported marker method or as plain structs, the state as a struct returned by value, a holder guarded by a sync.RWMutex (or a single owner goroutine fed by an event channel, following 'share memory by communicating'), and subscribers as per-subscriber channels or callbacks. Fan-out needs care because sends on a closed channel panic and a plain send blocks on a slow subscriber: remove the channel from the registry under the lock before closing it, and dispatch with select plus default or per-subscriber buffers, deliberately choosing to drop or to block. Nothing provides replay-1, so a new subscriber is handed the current snapshot at subscribe time.
pitfalls: Sending on a subscriber's channel after it is closed panics: remove the channel from the registry under the lock first, and never keep a stale reference in the dispatcher.
A plain send to an unread subscriber blocks the dispatcher and therefore every other update; use select with default, buffered channels, or a dedicated goroutine per subscriber - and document which.
Callbacks invoked while holding the lock deadlock the first time they re-enter Dispatch; snapshot the subscriber list (or the state) and call outside the critical section.
A state struct copied by value is safe to share only if it holds no maps or slices; deep-copy or replace such fields with immutable representations.
